company.name: Vink Holdings
company.description: Vink Holdings is a diversified holding company headquartered in Lusaka, Zambia, with operating subsidiaries across seven African markets. Since 2011 we have built and acquired businesses across real estate, financial services, agriculture, trading and distribution, energy and infrastructure, and hospitality — each run by a dedicated operating team with sector-specific expertise, reporting into a lean group centre focused on capital allocation, risk, and governance rather than day-to-day management. We'd rather be excellent at each of our six sectors than mediocre across all of them.

sectors.name: Real Estate & Development
sectors.shortDescription: 340,000 m² developed and held long-term across Zambia and DR Congo — not built to flip.
sectors.statLedSubhead: 340,000 m² of developed GLA. 94% occupancy. Six active developments — held, not flipped.
sectors.description: Vink Real Estate & Development plans, builds, and manages commercial, residential, and mixed-use assets across our operating markets. From grade-A office towers in Lusaka's Central Business District to affordable housing developments on the Copperbelt, our portfolio is built around long-term occupancy demand rather than speculative cycles. We hold assets through full-service management, not just development-and-exit — a 94% occupancy rate is the number that matters most here, and it's the one we lead with in every investor conversation about this sector, because it reflects tenants who stay, not just buildings that got built.
sectors.ctaLabel: Talk to Vink Properties About a Development →

sectors.name: Financial Services
sectors.shortDescription: 180,000+ active accounts, $42M loan book, three markets — reaching SMEs banks find too costly to serve.
sectors.statLedSubhead: 180,000+ active accounts. $42M loan book. Three markets. Serving the SMEs conventional banks find too costly to reach.
sectors.description: Vink Capital, Vink Microfinance, and Vink Pay give us three ways into the same underserved market: savings and lending, microfinance discipline, and modern payment rails. We combine traditional credit discipline with mobile wallets, agent banking, and card issuing — reaching customers other lenders write off as too expensive to serve, without relaxing underwriting standards. A 3.1% NPL ratio against a $42M book is the number that matters most here, and it's the one we lead with in every investor conversation about this sector.
sectors.ctaLabel: Talk to Vink Capital About a Partnership →

sectors.name: Agriculture & Agro-Processing
sectors.shortDescription: 6,200+ smallholder farmers under contract, 120,000 MT of annual processing capacity, three countries.
sectors.statLedSubhead: 6,200+ smallholder farmers under contract. 120,000 MT processing capacity a year. Three countries.
sectors.description: From contract farming with smallholders to large-scale commercial cultivation and processing, our agriculture businesses focus on staple crops, edible oils, and packaged foods for regional markets. We invest heavily in irrigation, storage, and processing capacity so that value — not just raw produce — stays within the countries we operate in. Our outgrower programme now supports more than 6,200 smallholder farmers across three countries with guaranteed offtake, agronomy training, and fair pricing — the structure we point to whenever a partner asks how we make food security commercially sustainable rather than charitable.
sectors.ctaLabel: Talk to Vink AgriProcessing About Sourcing →

sectors.name: Trading & Distribution
sectors.shortDescription: 85,000 m² of warehousing and 4,800+ retail touchpoints — the last-mile backbone for our own subsidiaries and third-party brands.
sectors.statLedSubhead: 85,000 m² of warehousing. 260+ fleet vehicles. 4,800+ retail touchpoints across five markets.
sectors.description: Our trading and distribution arm moves consumer goods, agricultural inputs, and industrial products through a network of warehouses, fleet, and retail partnerships spanning five countries. We act as the last-mile backbone for both our own subsidiaries and third-party brands entering the region — 4,800+ retail touchpoints served is the density figure that matters most here, because it's the difference between a distributor that can promise shelf coverage and one that can only promise a delivery date.
sectors.ctaLabel: Talk to Vink Logistics About Distribution →

sectors.name: Energy & Infrastructure
sectors.shortDescription: 38MW installed, 24,000 tCO₂e avoided annually — Phase II underway.
sectors.statLedSubhead: 38MW of installed solar capacity. 24,000 tCO₂e avoided a year. Phase II underway.
sectors.description: We invest in solar generation, mini-grids, and infrastructure that underpins growth in markets with unreliable grid access. Our energy projects range from commercial rooftop solar for our own real estate and agro-processing sites to independent power projects that feed surplus capacity back to national grids, alongside road and logistics infrastructure that de-risks trade corridors for the wider group. 38MW of installed capacity avoiding an estimated 24,000 tonnes of CO₂e annually is the figure we lead with — energy reliability is a precondition for almost everything else the group does, so investing in our own generation reduces cost and risk across every other sector we operate in.
sectors.ctaLabel: Talk to Vink Solar About a Project →

sectors.name: Hospitality & Services
sectors.shortDescription: 540 rooms under management and 90+ corporate service contracts across three markets.
sectors.statLedSubhead: 540 rooms under management. 90+ corporate service contracts. Three markets.
sectors.description: Our hospitality portfolio spans business hotels, serviced apartments, and event venues in the cities where our other businesses operate, supported by a professional services arm covering facilities, catering, and cleaning contracts for corporate clients. 90+ corporate service contracts is the number worth noting here: hospitality gives the group a direct, constant read on service quality standards that we then apply across every other customer-facing subsidiary — this sector is as much a quality-control function for the group as it is a business in its own right.

news.title: Vink Holdings Reports Strong Growth in 2024 Financial Year
news.excerpt: Vink Holdings closed the 2024 financial year with strong growth across its diversified portfolio, driven by disciplined execution across all six business sectors and continued expansion of subsidiary operations throughout the region.
news.body:
Vink Holdings closed the 2024 financial year with strong growth across its diversified portfolio, driven by disciplined execution across all six business sectors and continued expansion of subsidiary operations throughout the region.

Group revenue grew on the back of expanded lending activity in Financial Services, higher occupancy across the Real Estate & Development portfolio, and increased processing volumes in Agriculture & Agro-Processing. Trading & Distribution benefited from new distribution contracts secured in Mozambique and the Democratic Republic of Congo.

Management reiterated the group's long-term capital allocation discipline, noting that growth was achieved without a material increase in group leverage. The board has approved continued investment in the group's Energy & Infrastructure sector, including Phase II of the Vink Solar rooftop expansion programme.

The full FY2025 Annual Report is available to shareholders and analysts via the Investors section.

news.title: Investing in a Greener Tomorrow Through Renewable Energy
news.excerpt: As part of its long-term sustainability commitments, Vink Holdings is expanding its investment in renewable energy infrastructure, supporting the group's Energy & Infrastructure sector and reducing the environmental footprint of its operations.
news.body:
As part of its long-term sustainability commitments, Vink Holdings is expanding its investment in renewable energy infrastructure, supporting the group's Energy & Infrastructure sector and reducing the environmental footprint of its operations.

The group's installed solar capacity now stands at 38MW across rooftop and mini-grid installations in Zambia and Mozambique, avoiding an estimated 24,000 tonnes of CO₂e annually. Phase II of the expansion programme, backed by a recently closed $12M raise, will add rooftop capacity across additional real estate and agro-processing sites.

"Energy reliability is a precondition for almost everything else we do as a group," said Group Head of Sustainability Linda K. Phiri. "Investing in our own generation capacity reduces cost and risk across every other sector we operate in."

The programme is one of several initiatives outlined in the group's most recent ESG & Sustainability Report.

news.title: Empowering Communities, Transforming Lives
news.excerpt: Through its corporate social responsibility programmes, Vink Holdings continues to invest in the communities where it operates, focusing on education, enterprise development, and local job creation.
news.body:
Through its corporate social responsibility programmes, Vink Holdings continues to invest in the communities where it operates, focusing on education, enterprise development, and local job creation.

The group's outgrower programme now supports more than 6,200 smallholder farmers across Zambia, Zimbabwe, and Malawi, providing agronomy training, guaranteed offtake, and fair pricing. Beyond agriculture, group subsidiaries have funded scholarships, supported local vocational training centres, and prioritised local hiring across every market of operation.

"Our approach to community investment mirrors our approach to business — long-term, structured, and measured," said Group CEO M. Chanda Sakala. "We're not interested in one-off donations; we want programmes our subsidiaries still run in ten years."

Community investment activities are coordinated centrally but delivered locally by each subsidiary's operating team.

news.title: Vink Holdings Enters Kenya, Marking First East Africa Expansion
news.excerpt: The group has established two new subsidiaries in Nairobi, extending its regional footprint into East Africa for the first time and opening a new hub for Financial Services and Hospitality.
news.body:
The group has established two new subsidiaries in Nairobi, extending its regional footprint into East Africa for the first time and opening a new hub for Financial Services and Hospitality.

The Kenya entry follows two years of due diligence and regulatory engagement, and positions Nairobi as the group's East Africa base for future expansion. Vink Capital will offer SME and retail lending products, while the Hospitality & Services sector will manage a portfolio of serviced apartments targeting the city's growing corporate travel market.

"Kenya gives us a credible platform to serve East Africa the way we've served Southern Africa for over a decade," said COO Patrick O. Banda. The group is currently hiring across both new subsidiaries, with open roles listed on the Careers page.

news.title: Group ESG & Sustainability Report 2025 Published
news.excerpt: Vink Holdings has published its most comprehensive sustainability report to date, covering renewable energy, responsible agriculture, community investment, and governance across all operating markets.
news.body:
Vink Holdings has published its most comprehensive sustainability report to date, covering renewable energy, responsible agriculture, community investment, and governance across all operating markets.

The report details progress against the group's four sustainability pillars — renewable energy, responsible agriculture, community investment, and governance and compliance — with market-by-market data for the first time, reflecting the group's expanded footprint across seven countries.

The report is available for download via the Investors section alongside the group's financial disclosures.
